metadata.scope: First provenance-aware NTCP/xerostomia library for BioRT
metadata.clinical_use_warning: Decision support and model validation only. A model must not be used outside its endpoint, time point, structure definition, dose basis and treatment context without explicit review/recalibration.
metadata.selection_principle: Parameter sets are stored as indivisible model-specific records. Coefficients from different studies or time points must not be averaged or mixed.
metadata.runtime_selection_note: The implementation block is machine-readable and defines canonical structure, required input topology and runtime eligibility. Runtime eligibility does not imply clinical validation.
metadata.fractionation_note: Fractionation transforms are source-specific. Generic TG-166 per-bin LQED2 and source-reproduction transforms are represented separately and must not be interchanged.

lkb_probit.notes: v_i are differential fractional organ volumes. If n=1, Deff reduces to mean dose.

source.citation: Eisbruch A et al. Dose, volume, and function relationships in parotid salivary glands following conformal and intensity-modulated irradiation of head and neck cancer. IJROBP. 1999.

xerostomia_models.implementation_notes: Useful as a historical LKB benchmark. Endpoint/time-point definition must be reviewed from full text before clinical promotion.

implementation.runtime_reason: Historical benchmark only; endpoint/time-point definition is incomplete in the currently verified source extraction.

xerostomia_models.structure_definition: parotid gland; mean-organ-dose formulation with n fixed to 1

endpoint.name: xerostomia
endpoint.definition: stimulated salivary flow below 25% of pretreatment

dose_basis.fractionation_correction: For source datasets using fraction sizes other than 2 Gy, mean organ doses were converted to 2-Gy-fraction equivalent dose.

cohort.type: combined analysis of published multi-institutional clinical datasets

source.citation: Semenenko VA, Li XA. Lyman-Kutcher-Burman NTCP model parameters for radiation pneumonitis and xerostomia based on combined analysis of published clinical data. Phys Med Biol. 2008.

xerostomia_models.implementation_notes: Strong transparent classical reference. BioRT must apply the same fractionation convention if this parameter set is used.

implementation.fractionation_note: Reproduces the source convention: mean organ doses were converted to 2-Gy-fraction equivalent dose only for published cohorts using daily fractions other than 2 Gy. This is intentionally distinct from generic per-bin DVH LQED2 correction.

endpoint.name: parotid gland functional complication
endpoint.measurement: stimulated individual parotid flow using Lashley cups

parameters.n_provenance: mean-dose LKB formulation; n=1 is the equivalent LKB volume-effect assumption

dose_basis.metric: mean dose to individual parotid gland

source.citation: Dijkema T et al. Parotid gland function after radiotherapy: the combined Michigan and Utrecht experience. IJROBP. 2010.

xerostomia_models.implementation_notes: Endpoint is objective gland function at 1 year, not patient-rated xerostomia.

implementation.fractionation_note: Accessible abstract does not specify an explicit fractionation-normalization procedure; use outside conventional fractionation requires caution.

endpoint.name: parotid salivary flow recovery / xerostomia
endpoint.measurement: parotid saliva flow rate in PARSPORT

cohort.disease: locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

source.citation: Miah AB et al. Dose-response analysis of parotid gland function: what is the best measure of xerostomia? Radiother Oncol. 2013.

xerostomia_models.implementation_notes: The accessible abstract has a malformed/truncated confidence interval for m; the point estimate is retained but the m confidence interval is intentionally omitted pending full-text verification.

endpoint.name: moderate-to-severe xerostomia
endpoint.definition: grade 3+ xerostomia as defined by study

parameters.n_provenance: mean-dose/spared-gland implementation; retain as an explicit assumption until full-text equation verification

source.citation: Lee TF, Fang FM. QUANTEC guideline validation using quality-of-life questionnaire datasets for parotid gland constraints. Radiother Oncol. 2013.

xerostomia_models.implementation_notes: Do not merge with the 12-month fit. Time point is part of the model identity.

implementation.fractionation_note: Time-point-specific QoL fit; not interchangeable with the 12-month fit.

endpoint.name: moderate-to-severe xerostomia
endpoint.definition: grade 3+ xerostomia as defined by study

parameters.n_provenance: mean-dose/spared-gland implementation; retain as an explicit assumption until full-text equation verification

source.citation: Lee TF, Fang FM. QUANTEC guideline validation using quality-of-life questionnaire datasets for parotid gland constraints. Radiother Oncol. 2013.

xerostomia_models.implementation_notes: Do not merge with the 3-month fit. Time point is part of the model identity.

implementation.fractionation_note: Time-point-specific QoL fit; not interchangeable with the 3-month fit.

xerostomia_models.structure_definition: combined contralateral salivary glands: contralateral parotid + contralateral submandibular gland

endpoint.name: patient-reported xerostomia
endpoint.definition: increase in severity from baseline of at least 2

dose_basis.metric: dose-volume metrics of combined contralateral salivary glands

cohort.disease: favorable-risk HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
cohort.treatment: 60 Gy IMRT with concurrent weekly cisplatin

source.citation: Mavroidis P et al. Dose-volume toxicity modeling for de-intensified chemo-radiation therapy for HPV-positive oropharynx cancer. Radiother Oncol. 2017.

xerostomia_models.implementation_notes: Do not generalize automatically to standard-dose heterogeneous HNC populations.

implementation.runtime_reason: Requires a combined contralateral parotid + submandibular-gland dose representation and HPV+ de-intensified-treatment context.

source.citation: Beetz I et al. NTCP models for patient-rated xerostomia and sticky saliva after treatment with IMRT for head and neck cancer. Radiother Oncol. 2012.

xerostomia_models.implementation_notes: Transparent logistic comparator to LKB. Baseline symptom coding is mandatory.

implementation.runtime_note: Tumour laterality and baseline symptom status are required to identify the contralateral parotid and encode baseline xerostomia.

xerostomia_models.structure_definition: left and right parotid glands plus combined submandibular glands

endpoint.name: grade 2 or higher xerostomia
endpoint.measurement: EORTC QLQ-H&N35-derived endpoint in the LIPP development/validation framework

source.citation: Dalqvist E et al. Validated prediction of xerostomia in a real-world population: a step toward model-guided radiotherapy. Acta Oncol. 2025.

xerostomia_models.implementation_notes: This is a modern decision-support model, not an LKB parameter set. Local calibration must be checked before interpreting absolute risk.

implementation.runtime_note: Requires both parotids, combined submandibular dose, and baseline xerostomia category. Absolute-risk use also requires calibration review.

evidence_only.key_findings: 753 patients; grade >=2 and grade >=3 endpoints; Cox models using total or contralateral parotid mean dose plus clinical factors; risks estimated at 9, 12 and 24 months.
evidence_only.reason_not_computable_here: Multiple Cox models and nomograms; exact model choice and coefficient set require endpoint-specific extraction from tables/supplement before implementation.

evidence_only.key_findings: 231 favorable-risk HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer patients treated with 60 Gy IMRT; xerostomia modeled at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months using PRO-CTCAE and CTCAE; model results depend on scoring system, gland grouping and time point.
evidence_only.reason_not_computable_here: Accessible abstract does not expose the complete parameter table for every model/time point.

evidence_only.key_findings: Introduces a regeneration-weighted parotid dose and validates multivariable xerostomia models in 350 patients; supports future spatial-model branch.
evidence_only.reason_not_computable_here: Requires sub-parotid stem-cell-region segmentation and model-specific spatial dose metric not yet available in BioRT.

evidence_only.key_findings: 1208 patients from two institutions; moderate-to-severe xerostomia at 12 months; external validation highlights limited transportability and need for multicenter training/transfer learning.
evidence_only.reason_not_computable_here: Deep-learning model requires trained weights and multimodal 3D inputs; not a transparent coefficient model.

evidence_only.key_findings: Systematic review of studies from 2013-2025; 51 studies and 10,789 patients. Contralateral parotid mean dose remains the most consistently validated predictor; submandibular glands, oral cavity and parotid substructures provide additional information.
evidence_only.reason_not_computable_here: Evidence synthesis, not a single parameterized prediction model.

deprecated_or_invalid_composites.reason: Not traceable as a published indivisible parameter set. Numerically it matches approximately the arithmetic means of the separate 3-month and 12-month Lee/Fang 2013 fits (37.8/43.9 Gy and 0.59/0.48). Time-point-specific model parameters must not be averaged.
deprecated_or_invalid_composites.replacement: Select an explicit endpoint/time-point/model record from xerostomia_models.
